rules.rule_name: Retrieve Original Card Data as Baseline for Change Detection
rules.rule_description: When a user is in edit mode (card details already fetched and displayed), the system must establish the original card data as the baseline reference before comparing against any new values entered by the user. This baseline includes the Account ID, Card Number, Cardholder Name, Active Status, Expiry Day, Expiry Month, and Expiry Year as they were originally retrieved from the database.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Retrieve originally fetched card data
Card Name, Active Status,
Expiry Month, Expiry Year

acceptance_criteria.Given: The card details have already been fetched and displayed to the user, and the program is in edit mode (not in Details Not Fetched state)
acceptance_criteria.When: The user submits the screen with any input values
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system retrieves the originally fetched card data — Account ID (CCUP-OLD-ACCTID), Card Number (CCUP-OLD-CARDID), Cardholder Name (CCUP-OLD-CRDNAME), Active Status (CCUP-OLD-CRDSTCD), Expiry Day (CCUP-OLD-EXPDAY), Expiry Month (CCUP-OLD-EXPMON), and Expiry Year (CCUP-OLD-EXPYEAR) — and sets them as the reference baseline for comparison; additionally, the Account and Card filter flags are marked as valid since the card was already successfully retrieved

rules.rule_name: Case-Insensitive Comparison of New Card Data Against Original Card Data
rules.rule_description: The system performs a case-insensitive comparison of all editable card detail fields entered by the user against the original values that were displayed. The comparison treats uppercase and lowercase letters as equivalent, ensuring that a user typing a name in a different case does not trigger an unnecessary update.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Compare new card data
against original card data
Case-insensitive comparison

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has the original card data (CCUP-OLD-CARDDATA) as the baseline and the user has submitted new card data (CCUP-NEW-CARDDATA) on the screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The system compares the new card data against the original card data using a case-insensitive comparison (both sides converted to uppercase before comparison)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the uppercase version of the new card data exactly equals the uppercase version of the original card data, the system flags the state as 'No Changes Detected'; otherwise, the comparison proceeds to identify that changes have been made

rules.rule_name: Flag No Changes Detected When Submitted Data Matches Original Data
rules.rule_description: When the case-insensitive comparison determines that the user-submitted card data is identical to the originally displayed card data, the system sets a 'No Changes Detected' flag to indicate that no actual modification has been made by the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:

User submitted same values
as originally displayed

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has completed the case-insensitive comparison of new card data (CCUP-NEW-CARDDATA) against original card data (CCUP-OLD-CARDDATA)
acceptance_criteria.When: The uppercase value of CCUP-NEW-CARDDATA is equal to the uppercase value of CCUP-OLD-CARDDATA
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the state flag to 'No Changes Detected' (NO-CHANGES-DETECTED = TRUE), indicating the user has not modified any card detail fields

rules.rule_name: Bypass Field Validation When No Changes Detected, Confirmation Pending, or Update Already Completed
rules.rule_description: The system skips individual field-level validation for card details under three specific conditions: when no changes were detected, when changes have already been validated and are awaiting user confirmation (PF5), or when the update has already been successfully completed. In all three cases, all card detail fields are automatically marked as valid to avoid redundant re-validation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Is state: No Changes Detected
OR Changes Already Confirmed
OR Changes Already Done?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has evaluated the card data comparison result and determined the current program state
acceptance_criteria.When: The current state is any one of the following: (1) No Changes Detected (NO-CHANGES-DETECTED is TRUE), OR (2) Changes are valid and awaiting user confirmation (CCUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED is TRUE), OR (3) Changes have already been successfully saved (CCUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE is TRUE)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system marks all four card detail fields as valid — Cardholder Name (FLG-CARDNAME-ISVALID = TRUE), Active Status (FLG-CARDSTATUS-ISVALID = TRUE), Expiry Month (FLG-CARDEXPMON-ISVALID = TRUE), and Expiry Year (FLG-CARDEXPYEAR-ISVALID = TRUE) — and exits the validation process without performing any further field-level validation

rules.rule_name: Mark All Card Detail Fields as Valid and Skip Further Validation
rules.rule_description: When the system determines that field-level validation is not required (no changes detected, confirmation already pending, or update already done), it explicitly marks each of the four editable card detail fields as valid and terminates the validation process immediately, preventing unnecessary re-validation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:

Expiry Month, Expiry Year
No further validation needed

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has determined that field-level validation should be bypassed because the state is No Changes Detected, Changes OK Not Confirmed, or Changes Okayed and Done
acceptance_criteria.When: The bypass condition is met
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets FLG-CARDNAME-ISVALID to TRUE, FLG-CARDSTATUS-ISVALID to TRUE, FLG-CARDEXPMON-ISVALID to TRUE, and FLG-CARDEXPYEAR-ISVALID to TRUE, then immediately exits the input editing process without invoking any individual field validation routines

rules.rule_name: Mark State as Changes Not Yet Validated When Changes Are Detected
rules.rule_description: When the comparison reveals that the user has made changes to the card data, and the bypass conditions are not met, the system transitions the program state to 'Changes Not OK' to indicate that the detected changes have not yet been validated and must go through individual field validation before they can be confirmed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:

acceptance_criteria.Given: The case-insensitive comparison has determined that the new card data differs from the original card data, AND the current state is not No Changes Detected, not Changes OK Not Confirmed, and not Changes Okayed and Done
acceptance_criteria.When: Changes are detected and none of the bypass conditions apply
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the program state to 'Changes Not OK' (CCUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK = TRUE), signaling that the submitted changes require individual field-level validation before they can proceed to the confirmation step

rules.rule_name: Invoke Individual Field Validation for All Changed Card Detail Fields
rules.rule_description: When changes are detected and the state is set to 'Changes Not OK', the system sequentially invokes validation for each of the four editable card detail fields: Cardholder Name, Card Active Status, Expiry Month, and Expiry Year. All four validations are always performed regardless of whether earlier ones fail, ensuring complete error reporting to the user.

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program state has been set to 'Changes Not OK' because the user has submitted card data that differs from the original values
acceptance_criteria.When: The system proceeds to validate the changed card detail fields
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sequentially invokes validation for: (1) Cardholder Name validation (1230-EDIT-NAME), (2) Card Active Status validation (1240-EDIT-CARDSTATUS), (3) Expiry Month validation (1250-EDIT-EXPIRY-MON), and (4) Expiry Year validation (1260-EDIT-EXPIRY-YEAR) — all four validations are executed in order; if all pass, the state is promoted to 'Changes OK - Not Confirmed'; if any fail, the state remains 'Changes Not OK' with appropriate error indicators set

rules.rule_name: Mark Card Update State as Changes Not Yet Validated
rules.rule_description: When the user submits changed card details, the system immediately marks the update state as 'Changes Not Yet Validated' before performing any field-level validation, ensuring that no unvalidated changes can proceed to confirmation or saving.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark State as Changes Not Yet Validated

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is viewing card details on the Credit Card Update screen and has submitted changes to one or more editable fields (Card Name, Active Status, Expiry Month, or Expiry Year)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system detects that the submitted values differ from the original card details currently stored
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the program state to 'Changes Not Yet Validated' (CCUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK) before proceeding to validate each individual field, ensuring no changes are treated as valid until all validations pass

rules.rule_name: Card Name - Required Field Check
rules.rule_description: Validates that the Cardholder Name field is not left blank when the user submits card update changes. The card name is a mandatory field and must be provided before any update can proceed.

acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets an input error flag, marks the card name field status as blank/missing, and sets the informational message to prompt the user to enter a card name; validation of the card name field stops and processing continues to the next field (Card Active Status)

rules.rule_name: Card Name - Alphabetic Characters Only Check
rules.rule_description: Validates that the Cardholder Name contains only alphabetic characters. Names with numeric digits or non-alphabetic special characters are rejected to ensure data integrity of the embossed card name.

acceptance_criteria.Then: If non-alphabetic characters are found: the system sets an input error flag, marks the card name field as invalid, and sets the informational message to indicate the name must contain alphabetic characters only; if all characters are alphabetic: the card name is marked as valid and processing continues to the next field (Card Active Status)

rules.rule_name: Card Active Status - Required Field Check

acceptance_criteria.When: The Card Active Status field is blank, contains only spaces, or contains only zero values
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets an input error flag, marks the card status field as blank/missing, and sets the informational message to indicate that card status must be Y or N; validation of the status field stops and processing continues to the next field (Expiry Month)

rules.rule_name: Card Active Status - Valid Value Check (Y or N Only)

acceptance_criteria.When: The system checks whether the provided status value passes the Y-or-N validity check
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the value is not Y or N: the system sets an input error flag, marks the card status field as invalid, and sets the informational message to indicate that card status must be Y or N; if the value is Y or N: the card active status is marked as valid and processing continues to the next field (Expiry Month)

rules.rule_name: Card Expiry Month - Required Field Check

acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets an input error flag, marks the expiry month field as blank/missing, and sets the informational message to indicate that the expiry month is not valid; validation of the month field stops and processing continues to the next field (Expiry Year)

rules.rule_name: Card Expiry Month - Valid Calendar Month Range Check
rules.rule_description: Validates that the Card Expiry Month contains a valid calendar month value. Only values representing actual months of the year are accepted.

and between 1 and 12

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has provided a non-blank value in the Card Expiry Month field on the Credit Card Update screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The system checks whether the provided month value passes the valid-month condition (must be a numeric value representing a valid calendar month, i.e., 01 through 12)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the month is outside the valid range or is not numeric: the system sets an input error flag, marks the expiry month field as invalid, and sets the informational message to indicate that the expiry month is not valid; if the month is valid: the expiry month is marked as valid and processing continues to the next field (Expiry Year)

rules.rule_name: Card Expiry Year - Required Field Check
rules.rule_description: Validates that the Card Expiry Year field is not left blank when the user submits card update changes. The expiry year is a mandatory field for the card's expiration date.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
16: Card Expiry Year Validation
Is expiry year provided?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Credit Card Update screen in edit mode and has submitted changes
acceptance_criteria.When: The Card Expiry Year field is blank, contains only spaces, or contains only zero values
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets an input error flag, marks the expiry year field as blank/missing, and sets the informational message to indicate that the expiry year is not valid; validation of the year field stops and processing continues to the overall validation outcome check

rules.rule_name: Card Expiry Year - Valid Year Range Check
rules.rule_description: Validates that the Card Expiry Year contains a valid year value. Only years within an accepted range are permitted to ensure the expiry date is meaningful and within a reasonable business timeframe.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Check year is numeric
and between 1950 and 2099

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has provided a non-blank value in the Card Expiry Year field on the Credit Card Update screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The system checks whether the provided year value passes the valid-year condition (must be a numeric value within the accepted year range)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the year fails the validity check: the system sets an input error flag, marks the expiry year field as invalid, and sets the informational message to indicate that the expiry year is not valid; if the year is valid: the expiry year is marked as valid and processing continues to the overall validation outcome check

rules.rule_name: Determine Overall Validation Outcome - Errors Found
rules.rule_description: After all four card detail fields have been individually validated, the system evaluates the overall validation result. If any field failed validation, the update state remains as 'Changes Not Yet Validated' and the screen is redisplayed with all errors highlighted so the user can correct them.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Any Validation
Errors Found?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has completed validation of all four editable card fields: Card Name, Card Active Status, Expiry Month, and Expiry Year
acceptance_criteria.When: One or more of the validated fields has been flagged with an input error
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program state remains as 'Changes Not Yet Validated' (CCUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK); the screen is redisplayed with all invalid fields highlighted in red, blank required fields shown with an asterisk placeholder, and an appropriate error message prompting the user to correct the changes

rules.rule_name: Determine Overall Validation Outcome - All Fields Valid, Promote to Awaiting Confirmation
rules.rule_description: After all four card detail fields have been individually validated without any errors, the system promotes the update state to 'Changes OK - Awaiting Confirmation', protecting all fields from further editing and prompting the user to press PF5 to confirm and save the changes.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Promote State to
Changes OK - Awaiting Confirmation
Prompt user to confirm with PF05

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has completed validation of all four editable card fields: Card Name, Card Active Status, Expiry Month, and Expiry Year
acceptance_criteria.When: All four fields have passed their respective validations with no input errors detected
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program state is promoted to 'Changes OK - Not Confirmed' (CCUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED); all screen fields are set to protected (non-editable); the function key area is highlighted in bright yellow; and the informational message prompts the user to confirm the changes by pressing PF5

rules.rule_name: Determine Next Action Based on Current Program State
rules.rule_description: The system evaluates the current program state to determine which action path to follow. Each distinct state (details not fetched, details shown, changes with errors, changes pending confirmation, update completed) routes the program to a specific processing branch.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: What is the current program state?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Credit Card Update screen is active and the user has interacted with it by pressing a key or submitting data
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the current program state flag which can be one of: Details Not Yet Fetched, Card Details Currently Displayed, Changes Have Validation Errors, Changes OK Awaiting Confirmation, or Update Successfully Completed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system routes processing to the corresponding action branch for that state: search/lookup for Details Not Fetched, change detection for Show Details, error re-display for Changes Not OK, confirmation wait or save for Changes Pending Confirmation, or post-update display for Update Completed

rules.rule_name: Require Both Account Number and Card Number to Be Valid Before Card Lookup
rules.rule_description: When the program is in search mode (details not yet fetched) or a new search is requested via PF12, the system will only proceed to look up the card record if both the Account Number and the Card Number have passed their respective validation checks. If either is invalid, no lookup is attempted.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Are both Account Number and Card Number valid?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program state is Details Not Yet Fetched or the user has pressed PF12 to request a new search
acceptance_criteria.When: The system checks whether both the Account Number filter flag (FLG-ACCTFILTER-ISVALID) and the Card Number filter flag (FLG-CARDFILTER-ISVALID) are set to valid
acceptance_criteria.Then: If both are valid, the system proceeds to read the card record from the database; if either is invalid or blank, no database lookup is performed and the screen is re-displayed with existing error indicators

rules.rule_name: Read Card Details from Database Using Account and Card Number
rules.rule_description: When both search criteria are valid, the system retrieves the card record from the card database using the Card Number as the key. Upon successful retrieval, the card details including cardholder name (converted to uppercase), CVV code, expiry year, expiry month, expiry day, and active status are stored as the original reference values for subsequent comparison and display.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Read Card Details from Database

acceptance_criteria.Given: Both Account Number and Card Number have been validated as valid 11-digit and 16-digit numeric values respectively
acceptance_criteria.When: The system reads the card record from the card database file using the Card Number as the record identifier
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the card record is found, the system stores the following original values: CVV Code, Cardholder Name (converted to uppercase), Expiry Year (positions 1-4 of expiry date), Expiry Month (positions 6-7 of expiry date), Expiry Day (positions 9-10 of expiry date), and Card Active Status; these stored values serve as the baseline for change detection and concurrent update checking

rules.rule_name: Set Show Details State When Card Record Is Found
rules.rule_description: After attempting to read the card record from the database, if the record is successfully found, the program transitions to the Show Card Details state so the retrieved card information can be displayed to the user for review and editing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Card Record Found?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has attempted to read a card record from the database using the provided Account Number and Card Number
acceptance_criteria.When: The card record is successfully found in the database (normal response received)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program state is set to Show Card Details (CCUP-SHOW-DETAILS), and the screen will display the card's current details including cardholder name, active status, expiry month, expiry year, and expiry day

rules.rule_name: Display Error When Account and Card Number Combination Is Not Found
rules.rule_description: If the card record cannot be found in the database for the provided Account Number and Card Number combination, the system flags both the Account Number and Card Number fields as invalid and sets an error message indicating the combination was not found. The program remains in search mode.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Card Record Found? - Not Found

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has attempted to read a card record from the database using the provided Account Number and Card Number
acceptance_criteria.When: No matching card record is found in the database for the given combination
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets an input error condition, marks both the Account Number filter and Card Number filter as invalid (FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK and FLG-CARDFILTER-NOT-OK), and sets the error message to indicate that the account and card combination was not found; the program remains in search mode and re-displays the screen with both fields highlighted in error

rules.rule_name: Remain in Show Details State When No Changes Are Detected or Validation Errors Exist
rules.rule_description: When card details are currently displayed and the user submits the screen, if the submitted data is identical to the original data (no changes detected) or if there are input validation errors, the program remains in the Show Details state without advancing to the confirmation step.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Any input validation errors OR no changes detected?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program is in the Show Card Details state and the user has submitted the screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The system detects either that the submitted field values are identical to the original database values (case-insensitive comparison of all editable fields) OR that there are input validation errors present
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program remains in the Show Card Details state with no state change; the screen is re-displayed showing the current card details without advancing to the Changes Pending Confirmation state

rules.rule_name: Advance to Changes Pending Confirmation When Valid Changes Are Detected
rules.rule_description: When card details are displayed and the user submits changes that differ from the original values and all field validations pass, the program advances to the Changes Pending Confirmation state, requiring the user to explicitly confirm before the update is saved.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Any input validation errors OR no changes detected? - No Changes Detected

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program is in the Show Card Details state and the user has submitted the screen with modified field values
acceptance_criteria.When: The submitted data differs from the original database values (at least one of: cardholder name, card status, expiry month, or expiry year has changed) AND there are no input validation errors on any field
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program state is set to Changes OK - Not Confirmed (CCUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED), all editable fields become protected on screen, and the user is prompted to press PF5 to confirm the changes or PF3 to cancel

rules.rule_name: Remain in Error State When Changes Have Validation Failures
rules.rule_description: When the program is in the Changes Have Validation Errors state, no further processing action is taken in the decision logic. The program remains in this state and the screen will be re-displayed with error highlights on the invalid fields.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: State: Changes Have Validation Errors

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program is in the Changes Have Validation Errors state (CCUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK) because one or more of the submitted field values failed validation
acceptance_criteria.When: The action decision logic evaluates the current state
acceptance_criteria.Then: No state change occurs; the program remains in the Changes Not OK state and proceeds to re-display the screen with all invalid fields highlighted in red, asterisks shown for blank required fields, and appropriate error messages

rules.rule_name: Wait for User Confirmation When PF5 Has Not Been Pressed
rules.rule_description: When the program is in the Changes OK Awaiting Confirmation state but the user has not pressed PF5, no save action is taken. The program remains in the confirmation-pending state, keeping all fields protected and continuing to prompt the user for confirmation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Did user press PF05 to Confirm? - No

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program is in the Changes OK - Not Confirmed state (CCUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED) with valid pending changes awaiting user confirmation
acceptance_criteria.When: The user submits the screen without pressing PF5 (e.g., presses ENTER or another non-PF5 key)
acceptance_criteria.Then: No save operation is initiated; the program remains in the Changes OK - Not Confirmed state, all fields remain protected, the PF key area remains highlighted in bright yellow, and the confirmation prompt message continues to be displayed

rules.rule_name: Initiate Card Update Save When User Confirms with PF5
rules.rule_description: When the program is in the Changes OK Awaiting Confirmation state and the user presses PF5, the system initiates the write processing to save the card updates to the database. This triggers the full save workflow including record locking and concurrent update checking.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Did user press PF05 to Confirm? - Yes

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program is in the Changes OK - Not Confirmed state (CCUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED) with valid pending changes
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses PF5 to confirm the changes
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system invokes the write processing routine (9200-WRITE-PROCESSING) to attempt to lock the card record and save the updated values to the database; the outcome of the save attempt determines the next program state

rules.rule_name: Set Lock Error State When Card Record Cannot Be Locked for Update
rules.rule_description: During the save attempt, if the system is unable to obtain an exclusive lock on the card record (because another user or process has it locked), the program transitions to the Lock Error state and an appropriate failure message is displayed to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set State: Lock Error - Could Not Save

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has attempted to lock the card record for update as part of the save processing initiated by the user pressing PF5
acceptance_criteria.When: The database returns a non-normal response when attempting to read the card record with an update lock (COULD-NOT-LOCK-FOR-UPDATE condition is set)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program state is set to Changes Okayed - Lock Error (CCUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-LOCK-ERROR), the save is not completed, and a failure message is displayed to inform the user that the record could not be saved

rules.rule_name: Set Update Failed State When Record Is Locked But Write Operation Fails
rules.rule_description: During the save attempt, if the system successfully locks the card record but the subsequent rewrite operation fails, the program transitions to the Update Failed state and a failure message is displayed to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set State: Update Failed

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has successfully locked the card record for update and has attempted to rewrite the updated card record to the database
acceptance_criteria.When: The rewrite operation returns a non-normal response (LOCKED-BUT-UPDATE-FAILED condition is set)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program state is set to Changes Okayed But Failed (CCUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-BUT-FAILED), the update is not completed, and a failure message is displayed to inform the user that the save operation was unsuccessful

rules.rule_name: Refresh Card Details When Record Was Modified by Another User Before Save
rules.rule_description: During the save attempt, after locking the record, the system compares the currently locked record against the values that were originally displayed to the user. If any field has been changed by another user or process in the interim, the save is aborted and the screen is refreshed with the latest database values so the user can review the current state before re-confirming.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set State: Data Changed by Another User - Refresh with Latest Data

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has successfully locked the card record for update and is performing a concurrent update check by comparing the locked record's current values against the values originally shown to the user (CVV code, cardholder name, expiry year, expiry month, expiry day, and active status)
acceptance_criteria.When: Any of the compared fields differ between the currently locked database record and the values that were originally displayed to the user (DATA-WAS-CHANGED-BEFORE-UPDATE condition is set), indicating another user or process modified the record
acceptance_criteria.Then: The save operation is aborted without writing any changes; the program state is set to Show Card Details (CCUP-SHOW-DETAILS) with the latest values from the database (updated CVV, name, expiry year, month, day, and status) so the user can review the current record and decide whether to re-submit their changes

rules.rule_name: Set Update Successfully Completed State After Successful Save
rules.rule_description: When the card record is successfully locked, passes the concurrent update check, and the rewrite operation completes normally, the program transitions to the Update Successfully Completed state and a success confirmation message is displayed to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set State: Update Successfully Completed

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has successfully locked the card record, confirmed no concurrent modifications occurred, and has rewritten the updated card record to the database
acceptance_criteria.When: The rewrite operation returns a normal successful response (none of the error conditions COULD-NOT-LOCK-FOR-UPDATE, LOCKED-BUT-UPDATE-FAILED, or DATA-WAS-CHANGED-BEFORE-UPDATE are set)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program state is set to Changes Okayed and Done (CCUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE), and a success confirmation message is displayed to the user indicating the card update was completed successfully

rules.rule_name: Clear Account and Card Number References When No Return Transaction Is Set After Successful Update
rules.rule_description: After a successful card update, if the program was not called from another transaction (no originating transaction ID is recorded in the session), the Account ID and Card Number references in the session are cleared to prevent stale data from persisting.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Was this called from another transaction? - No Return Transaction Set

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program state is Update Successfully Completed (CCUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE)
acceptance_criteria.When: The originating transaction ID (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID) is equal to LOW-VALUES or spaces, indicating the program was not called from another transaction
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Account ID (CDEMO-ACCT-ID) is set to zeros, the Card Number (CDEMO-CARD-NUM) is set to zeros, and the Account Status (CDEMO-ACCT-STATUS) is set to LOW-VALUES to clear these session references

rules.rule_name: Display Updated Card Details After Successful Update
rules.rule_description: After a successful card update, regardless of whether the program was called from another transaction, the program transitions to the Show Card Details state so the user can see the result of their successful update on screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set State: Show Updated Card Details

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program state is Update Successfully Completed (CCUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE) following a successful save of card updates
acceptance_criteria.When: The action decision logic processes the Update Completed state
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program state is set to Show Card Details (CCUP-SHOW-DETAILS) so the screen will display the updated card information, and a success confirmation message is shown to the user

sub_functionalities.title: Attempt to Save Card Updates to Database
sub_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Start: User Confirmed Changes\nPF05 Pressed]) 
    B[Attempt to Lock\nCard Record for Update]
    C{Record\nLocked\nSuccessfully?}

    E[Compare Current Database Values\nAgainst Originally Displayed Values:\nCard Name, CVV, Expiry Date,\nActive Status]
    F{Has Another User\nModified This Record\nSince It Was Displayed?}

    H[Prepare Updated Card Record:\n- New Card Name\n- New Expiry Date formatted YYYY-MM-DD\n- New Active Status Y or N\n- CVV Code]
    I[Write Updated Card Record\nTo Card Database]
    J{Write\nSuccessful?}
    K[Set Update Success Status\nChanges Saved to Database]
    L[Set Update Failed Status\nRecord Was Locked But\nCould Not Be Saved]
    M{Evaluate\nFinal Outcome}
    N([End: Lock Error\nInform User of Failure])
    O([End: Concurrent Change\nShow Refreshed Card Details\nPrompt User to Re-enter Changes])
    P([End: Update Success\nConfirm Changes Saved])
    Q([End: Update Failed\nInform User of Failure])

    A --> B
    B --> C
    C -->|No - Record Unavailable| D
    D --> M
    C -->|Yes - Record Locked| E
    E --> F
    F -->|Yes - Concurrent Change Detected| G
    G --> M
    F -->|No - Record Unchanged| H
    H --> I
    I --> J
    J -->|Yes| K
    K --> M
    J -->|No| L
    L --> M
    M -->|Lock Error| N
    M -->|Concurrent Change| O
    M -->|Success| P
    M -->|Update Failed| Q

rules.rule_name: Lock Card Record Before Update
rules.rule_description: Before any card update can be performed, the system must exclusively lock the card record in the database using the card number as the key. This prevents other users from modifying the same record simultaneously during the update process.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Attempt to Lock Card Record for Update

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has confirmed their card changes by pressing PF5, and the card number is available in the current session
acceptance_criteria.When: The system attempts to retrieve and lock the card record from the Card Database using the Card Number as the unique identifier
acceptance_criteria.Then: The card record is locked exclusively for update using the Card Number as the lookup key, preventing any other user from modifying the same record until the update is complete or released

rules.rule_name: Handle Record Lock Failure
rules.rule_description: If the card record cannot be locked for update — because it is already held by another process or is otherwise unavailable — the update must be aborted and the user must be informed of the failure.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Record Locked Successfully? → No - Record Unavailable → Set Lock Error Status Update Cannot Proceed

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has confirmed their card changes by pressing PF5 and the system has attempted to lock the card record
acceptance_criteria.When: The card record cannot be locked because it is currently unavailable or held by another process
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the status to 'Could Not Lock For Update', marks the input as an error, and the update does not proceed; the final outcome is evaluated as a Lock Error and the user is informed of the failure

rules.rule_name: Detect Concurrent Modification of Card Record
rules.rule_description: After successfully locking the card record, the system must verify that no other user has changed the record between the time it was originally displayed to the current user and the time the update is being applied. This is done by comparing the current database values against the values that were originally shown to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Compare Current Database Values Against Originally Displayed Values: Card Name, CVV, Expiry Date, Active Status

acceptance_criteria.Given: The card record has been successfully locked for update, and the system has the original values that were displayed to the user (Card Name, CVV Code, Expiry Year, Expiry Month, Expiry Day, Active Status)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system compares the current database values of the card record against the originally displayed values for all of the following fields: CVV Code, Cardholder Name (converted to uppercase), Expiry Year (positions 1–4 of expiry date), Expiry Month (positions 6–7 of expiry date), Expiry Day (positions 9–10 of expiry date), and Active Status
acceptance_criteria.Then: If all six fields match exactly between the current database record and the originally displayed values, no concurrent modification is detected and the update proceeds; if any single field differs, a concurrent modification is detected and the update is aborted

rules.rule_name: Abort Update and Refresh Card Data on Concurrent Change
rules.rule_description: When a concurrent modification is detected — meaning another user changed the card record after it was displayed to the current user — the current update must be aborted. The screen must be refreshed with the latest values from the database so the user can review the current state and re-enter their changes.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Has Another User Modified This Record Since It Was Displayed? → Yes - Concurrent Change Detected → Refresh Screen With Latest Card Data From Database Abort Current Update

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has detected that the card record was modified by another user after it was originally displayed, by finding at least one difference in CVV Code, Cardholder Name, Expiry Year, Expiry Month, Expiry Day, or Active Status
acceptance_criteria.When: The concurrent modification is confirmed and the current update is aborted
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the status to 'Data Was Changed Before Update', refreshes the stored original values with the latest database values for CVV Code, Cardholder Name, Expiry Year, Expiry Month, Expiry Day, and Active Status, and the final outcome is evaluated as a Concurrent Change; the screen is re-displayed with the latest card details and the user is prompted to re-enter their changes

rules.rule_name: Prepare Updated Card Record with New Field Values
rules.rule_description: When no concurrent modification is detected, the system prepares the updated card record by assembling the new values entered by the user alongside the unchanged values carried forward from the original record. The update record is initialized before being populated.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Prepare Updated Card Record: - New Card Name - New Expiry Date formatted YYYY-MM-DD - New Active Status Y or N - CVV Code

acceptance_criteria.Given: No concurrent modification has been detected and the update is cleared to proceed
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the updated card record for writing to the database
acceptance_criteria.Then: The updated card record is assembled with the following values: Card Number (new value from user input), Account ID (from current session, numeric format), CVV Code (carried forward unchanged from the original record), Cardholder Name (new value entered by user), and Active Status (new value entered by user, Y or N)

rules.rule_name: Format Expiry Date as YYYY-MM-DD Preserving Original Day
rules.rule_description: The expiry date stored in the database must always follow the YYYY-MM-DD format. When preparing the update, the expiry year and expiry month come from the new values entered by the user, but the expiry day is always carried forward from the original record because the user is not permitted to change the expiry day.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Prepare Updated Card Record: - New Expiry Date formatted YYYY-MM-DD

acceptance_criteria.Given: The updated card record is being prepared and the user has provided a new Expiry Year and new Expiry Month, while the original Expiry Day is retained from the originally displayed record
acceptance_criteria.When: The system constructs the expiry date field for the updated card record
acceptance_criteria.Then: The expiry date is formatted as YYYY-MM-DD by concatenating: the new Expiry Year (4 digits), a hyphen '-', the new Expiry Month (2 digits), a hyphen '-', and the original Expiry Day (2 digits, unchanged from the original record); the resulting date string is stored in the Card Expiry Date field of the update record

rules.rule_name: Write Updated Card Record to Database
rules.rule_description: After the updated card record has been fully prepared with all new and carried-forward values, the system writes the updated record back to the Card Database, replacing the previously locked record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Write Updated Card Record To Card Database

acceptance_criteria.Given: The updated card record has been fully prepared with the new Card Name, formatted Expiry Date, new Active Status, carried-forward CVV Code, Card Number, and Account ID
acceptance_criteria.When: The system writes the updated card record to the Card Database to replace the existing locked record
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Card Database record is rewritten with the updated card record; the outcome of the write operation (success or failure) is captured for subsequent evaluation

rules.rule_name: Confirm Successful Card Update
rules.rule_description: When the write operation to the Card Database completes successfully, the system sets the program state to indicate that the changes have been saved, and the user is shown a success confirmation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Write Successful? → Yes → Set Update Success Status Changes Saved to Database

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has attempted to write the updated card record to the Card Database
acceptance_criteria.When: The write operation completes successfully with a normal response
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the status to 'Changes Okayed and Done'; the final outcome is evaluated as Update Success and the user is shown a confirmation that the changes have been saved to the database

rules.rule_name: Handle Write Failure After Successful Lock
rules.rule_description: If the card record was successfully locked but the subsequent write operation fails, the system must set a specific failure status to distinguish this scenario from a lock failure. The user is informed that the update could not be completed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Write Successful? → No → Set Update Failed Status Record Was Locked But Could Not Be Saved

acceptance_criteria.Given: The card record was successfully locked for update and the updated record was prepared, but the write operation to the Card Database did not complete successfully
acceptance_criteria.When: The write operation returns a non-normal response
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the status to 'Locked But Update Failed'; the final outcome is evaluated as Update Failed and the user is informed of the failure

rules.rule_name: Evaluate and Route Final Update Outcome to Appropriate End State
rules.rule_description: After the write processing completes, the system evaluates the final outcome status and routes the program to the appropriate end state, each with a distinct user-facing result: lock error, concurrent change, success, or update failure.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Evaluate Final Outcome

acceptance_criteria.Given: The write processing has completed and a final outcome status has been set: one of 'Could Not Lock For Update', 'Data Was Changed Before Update', 'Changes Okayed and Done', or 'Locked But Update Failed'
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the final outcome status
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system routes to the appropriate end state as follows: if the status is 'Could Not Lock For Update' then the program state is set to 'Changes Okayed Lock Error' and the user is informed of a lock failure; if the status is 'Data Was Changed Before Update' then the program state is set to 'Show Details' and the screen is refreshed with the latest card data prompting the user to re-enter changes; if the status is 'Changes Okayed and Done' (normal write success) then the program state remains 'Changes Okayed and Done' and the user receives a success confirmation; if the status is 'Locked But Update Failed' then the program state is set to 'Changes Okayed But Failed' and the user is informed of the failure

rules.rule_name: Clear Previously Held Card Details Before New Search
rules.rule_description: Before initiating a new card data retrieval, all previously stored card detail fields must be cleared to ensure no stale data from a prior lookup is retained or displayed to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Clear previously held card details storage

acceptance_criteria.Given: A request has been made to read card data for display, and the card details storage area may contain data from a previous lookup
acceptance_criteria.When: The card data read process is initiated
acceptance_criteria.Then: All previously held card detail fields (including old account ID, card ID, CVV code, cardholder name, expiry year, expiry month, expiry day, and card active status) are cleared and reset to their initial empty state before any new search is performed

rules.rule_name: Set Account Number and Card Number as Search Keys for Card Lookup
rules.rule_description: Prior to searching the card database, the system must establish the account number and card number as the search identifiers to be used in the lookup operation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set account number and card number as search keys

acceptance_criteria.Given: The card details storage has been cleared and a valid Account ID and Card Number are available in the current session
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to search the card database
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Account ID from the current session is stored as the old account ID search key, and the Card Number from the current session is stored as the old card ID search key, making both values available for the database lookup and for subsequent comparison operations

rules.rule_name: Search Card Database Using Card Number as the Primary Key
rules.rule_description: The card database (CARDDAT) must be searched using the Card Number as the unique retrieval key to locate the specific card record for display.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Search card database using card number as the key

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account ID and Card Number have been set as search keys, and the card database (CARDDAT) is accessible
acceptance_criteria.When: The system performs the card database lookup
acceptance_criteria.Then: The card database is searched using the full Card Number as the key, retrieving the complete card record including cardholder name, CVV code, expiry date, and active status; the search result determines the subsequent processing path (card found, card not found, or retrieval issue)

rules.rule_name: Populate Card Details Upon Successful Card Record Retrieval
rules.rule_description: When a card record is successfully located in the card database, all relevant card detail fields must be extracted from the retrieved record and stored for display to the user, with the cardholder name converted to uppercase.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Card record successfully located

acceptance_criteria.Given: A search of the card database using the Card Number has been performed
acceptance_criteria.When: The card record is successfully found and retrieved from the card database
acceptance_criteria.Then: The following card details are extracted from the retrieved record and stored as the current card details for display: CVV code is stored as-is; cardholder name is converted to uppercase before storing; expiry year is extracted from positions 1 through 4 of the expiry date field; expiry month is extracted from positions 6 through 7 of the expiry date field; expiry day is extracted from positions 9 through 10 of the expiry date field; and card active status is stored as-is

rules.rule_name: Convert Cardholder Name to Uppercase on Retrieval
rules.rule_description: When a card record is successfully retrieved from the database, the cardholder name (card embossed name) must be standardized to uppercase before being stored and displayed, ensuring consistent presentation regardless of how the name was originally stored.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Card record successfully located

acceptance_criteria.Given: A card record has been successfully retrieved from the card database and the cardholder name field contains the embossed name as stored in the database
acceptance_criteria.When: The system processes the retrieved card record for display
acceptance_criteria.Then: All lowercase alphabetic characters in the cardholder name are converted to their uppercase equivalents before the name is stored in the card details display area, ensuring the name is always presented in uppercase to the user

rules.rule_name: Handle Card Not Found - Account and Card Number Combination Does Not Exist
rules.rule_description: When the card database search returns no matching record for the provided Card Number, the system must flag both the account and card number inputs as invalid and inform the user that the combination was not found.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Card not found for the given account and card number / Set error flag: Account and card number combination not found / Display error message to user

acceptance_criteria.Given: A search of the card database using the provided Card Number has been performed
acceptance_criteria.When: The card database returns a 'not found' result, meaning no card record exists for the given Card Number
acceptance_criteria.Then: An input error flag is set to indicate invalid input; both the account number filter flag and the card number filter flag are marked as invalid; and if no prior error message has already been set, an error message is displayed to the user indicating that the account and card number combination was not found in the system

rules.rule_name: Handle Card Retrieval System Issue - Unable to Retrieve Card Details
rules.rule_description: When the card database search encounters an unexpected issue (neither a successful retrieval nor a standard not-found response), the system must flag the account number as invalid and display a system error message to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set error flag: Unable to retrieve card details / Display error message to user

acceptance_criteria.Given: A search of the card database using the provided Card Number has been performed
acceptance_criteria.When: The card database returns an unexpected result that is neither a successful retrieval nor a standard not-found response
acceptance_criteria.Then: An input error flag is set to indicate invalid input; the account number filter flag is marked as invalid; and if no prior error message has already been set, a file error message is displayed to the user indicating that the card details could not be retrieved, including the operation name, the file name, and the specific error response details

rules.rule_name: CVV Security Code Extraction and Storage After Card Retrieval
rules.rule_description: When a card record is successfully retrieved from the database, the CVV security code must be extracted from the card record and stored in the old-details holding area so it can be preserved and carried forward during any subsequent update operation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Extract CVV Security Code
from card record
Store in old-details holding area

acceptance_criteria.Given: A card record has been successfully retrieved from the card database using the provided Account ID and Card Number combination
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the card data for display by populating the old-details holding area
acceptance_criteria.Then: The CVV security code is extracted from the retrieved card record and stored in the old-details holding area field CCUP-OLD-CVV-CD, preserving the original value for use during update processing

rules.rule_name: Cardholder Embossed Name Conversion to Uppercase
rules.rule_description: The cardholder embossed name retrieved from the card record must be converted entirely to uppercase letters before being stored or displayed, ensuring consistent name formatting across all card update operations.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Convert Embossed Card Name
to Uppercase

acceptance_criteria.Given: A card record has been successfully retrieved from the card database and the embossed cardholder name is available in the card record
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the card data for display
acceptance_criteria.Then: All lowercase alphabetic characters in the embossed cardholder name are converted to their uppercase equivalents, so that the name is stored and displayed entirely in uppercase format

rules.rule_name: Uppercase Cardholder Name Storage in Old-Details Holding Area
rules.rule_description: After the embossed cardholder name has been converted to uppercase, the uppercase version must be stored in the old-details holding area so it can be displayed to the user and used as the baseline for detecting any changes made during the update session.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Store Uppercase Card Name
in old-details holding area

acceptance_criteria.Given: The embossed cardholder name from the retrieved card record has been converted to uppercase
acceptance_criteria.When: The system stores the card details into the old-details holding area
acceptance_criteria.Then: The uppercase version of the embossed cardholder name is stored in the old-details holding area field CCUP-OLD-CRDNAME, making it available for display and for change-detection comparison during the update workflow

rules.rule_name: Card Expiry Year Extraction from Expiry Date
rules.rule_description: The card expiry date is stored in the database as a formatted date string. The expiry year component, occupying the first four characters (positions 1 through 4) of the expiry date field, must be extracted separately and stored in the old-details holding area for individual field display and validation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Extract Expiry Year
from expiry date positions 1 to 4
Store in old-details holding area

acceptance_criteria.Given: A card record has been successfully retrieved and the card expiry date is available in YYYY-MM-DD format within the card record
acceptance_criteria.When: The system extracts individual date components from the expiry date field
acceptance_criteria.Then: The four-character year value is extracted from positions 1 through 4 of the expiry date field and stored in the old-details holding area field CCUP-OLD-EXPYEAR, representing the four-digit expiry year (e.g., 2027)

rules.rule_name: Card Expiry Month Extraction from Expiry Date
rules.rule_description: The expiry month component, occupying two characters at positions 6 through 7 of the expiry date field (after the year and separator), must be extracted separately and stored in the old-details holding area for individual field display and validation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Extract Expiry Month
from expiry date positions 6 to 7
Store in old-details holding area

acceptance_criteria.Given: A card record has been successfully retrieved and the card expiry date is available in YYYY-MM-DD format within the card record
acceptance_criteria.When: The system extracts individual date components from the expiry date field
acceptance_criteria.Then: The two-character month value is extracted from positions 6 through 7 of the expiry date field and stored in the old-details holding area field CCUP-OLD-EXPMON, representing the two-digit expiry month (e.g., 01 through 12)

rules.rule_name: Card Expiry Day Extraction from Expiry Date
rules.rule_description: The expiry day component, occupying two characters at positions 9 through 10 of the expiry date field, must be extracted separately and stored in the old-details holding area. The expiry day is a display-only value that cannot be modified by the user and is always carried forward unchanged during any update.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Extract Expiry Day
from expiry date positions 9 to 10
Store in old-details holding area

acceptance_criteria.Given: A card record has been successfully retrieved and the card expiry date is available in YYYY-MM-DD format within the card record
acceptance_criteria.When: The system extracts individual date components from the expiry date field
acceptance_criteria.Then: The two-character day value is extracted from positions 9 through 10 of the expiry date field and stored in the old-details holding area field CCUP-OLD-EXPDAY, representing the two-digit expiry day; this value is read-only and will be preserved unchanged in any subsequent update to the card record

rules.rule_name: Card Active Status Extraction and Storage in Old-Details Holding Area
rules.rule_description: The card active status indicator from the retrieved card record must be extracted and stored in the old-details holding area. This status indicates whether the card is currently active (Y) or inactive (N) and serves as the baseline value for display and change detection during the update session.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Extract Card Active Status
Y for Active or N for Inactive
Store in old-details holding area

acceptance_criteria.Given: A card record has been successfully retrieved from the card database
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the card data for display by populating the old-details holding area
acceptance_criteria.Then: The card active status value is extracted from the card record and stored in the old-details holding area field CCUP-OLD-CRDSTCD; the value is Y indicating the card is Active, or N indicating the card is Inactive, and this value is used as the baseline for detecting user-initiated status changes

rules.rule_name: Acquire Exclusive Lock on Card Record Before Update
rules.rule_description: Before saving any changes to a credit card record, the system must re-read the card record from the Card File using the Card Number as the unique key and request an exclusive update lock to prevent simultaneous modifications by other users.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Re-read Card Record from Database Using Card Number as Key Request Exclusive Lock for Update

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has confirmed pending changes to a credit card record and the Card Number is available as the record key
acceptance_criteria.When: The system attempts to re-read the card record from the Card File with an exclusive update lock using the Card Number as the lookup key
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system retrieves the latest version of the card record from the Card File and holds an exclusive lock on it, preventing other users from modifying the same record until the update is complete or released

rules.rule_name: Reject Update When Card Record Cannot Be Locked
rules.rule_description: If the system is unable to acquire an exclusive lock on the card record during the update attempt, the update process must be immediately halted and the user must be informed that the record could not be locked.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Lock Acquired Successfully?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has confirmed pending changes to a credit card record and the system has attempted to re-read the card record with an exclusive update lock
acceptance_criteria.When: The lock acquisition fails because the card record is unavailable or already locked by another process
acceptance_criteria.Then: The update process is immediately stopped, the system sets the status to 'Could Not Lock for Update', and the user is informed of the failure so they may retry the operation

rules.rule_name: Normalize Card Name to Uppercase Before Comparison
rules.rule_description: Before comparing the current database card name against the originally fetched card name, the card name retrieved from the database must be converted to uppercase to ensure a case-insensitive and consistent comparison.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Convert Card Name to Uppercase for Comparison

acceptance_criteria.Given: The card record has been successfully re-read from the Card File with an exclusive lock and the card name field contains the current database value in any mix of upper and lower case
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to compare the current database card name against the originally displayed card name
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system converts all lowercase letters in the current database card name to uppercase before performing the comparison, ensuring the comparison is not affected by letter casing differences

rules.rule_name: Detect Concurrent Modification by Comparing All Card Fields
rules.rule_description: After acquiring the exclusive lock, the system must compare all key card fields from the current database record against the values that were originally displayed to the user. If any field differs, it means another user has modified the record in the meantime and the update must be blocked.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Compare Current Database Values against Originally Fetched Values: CVV Code matches? Card Name matches? Expiry Year matches? Expiry Month matches? Expiry Day matches? Active Status matches?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The card record has been successfully re-read and locked, and the system holds the originally fetched card values (CVV Code, Card Name, Expiry Year, Expiry Month, Expiry Day, Active Status) from when the card was first displayed to the user
acceptance_criteria.When: The system compares the current database values against the originally fetched values for all six fields: CVV Code, Card Name (uppercase), Expiry Year (positions 1-4 of expiry date), Expiry Month (positions 6-7 of expiry date), Expiry Day (positions 9-10 of expiry date), and Active Status
acceptance_criteria.Then: If all six fields match exactly, no concurrent modification is detected and the system proceeds to apply the user's changes; if any one or more fields differ, a concurrent modification is detected and the update is blocked

rules.rule_name: Refresh Stored Original Card Details When Concurrent Modification Is Detected
rules.rule_description: When a concurrent modification is detected, the system must update its internally stored 'original' card details with the latest values from the database so that the refreshed screen accurately reflects the most current state of the card record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Refresh Stored Original Details with Latest Database Values: Update CVV, Card Name, Expiry Year, Month, Day, Active Status

acceptance_criteria.Given: A concurrent modification has been detected because one or more of the six compared fields (CVV Code, Card Name, Expiry Year, Expiry Month, Expiry Day, Active Status) differ between the current database record and the originally fetched values
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to re-display the card details to the user with the latest data
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system overwrites the stored original card details with the latest values from the database for all six fields: CVV Code is updated from the current database CVV, Card Name is updated from the current database card name (uppercase), Expiry Year is updated from positions 1-4 of the current expiry date, Expiry Month is updated from positions 6-7 of the current expiry date, Expiry Day is updated from positions 9-10 of the current expiry date, and Active Status is updated from the current database active status

rules.rule_name: Block Update and Redisplay Refreshed Card Details After Concurrent Modification
rules.rule_description: When a concurrent modification is detected, the pending update must be cancelled and the screen must be returned to the Show Details state so the user can review the latest card data before deciding whether to re-submit their changes.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Exit: Data Changed by Another User Display Refreshed Card Details to User

acceptance_criteria.Given: A concurrent modification has been detected and the stored original card details have been refreshed with the latest database values
acceptance_criteria.When: The system determines the outcome of the write processing attempt
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the program state to 'Show Details' (CCUP-SHOW-DETAILS), cancels the pending update, and redisplays the card detail screen populated with the latest database values so the user can review the changes made by the other user before deciding to re-enter and re-confirm their own changes

rules.rule_name: Proceed to Confirm Successful Update When No Concurrent Modification Detected
rules.rule_description: When all six compared fields match between the current database record and the originally fetched values, confirming no concurrent modification has occurred, the system proceeds to apply the user's changes and marks the update as successfully completed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Proceed to Card Record Update No Concurrent Changes Detected

acceptance_criteria.Given: All six fields (CVV Code, Card Name, Expiry Year, Expiry Month, Expiry Day, Active Status) match exactly between the current database record and the originally fetched values, and the card record rewrite to the Card File has completed without error
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the outcome of the write processing
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the program state to 'Changes Okayed and Done' (CCUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE), confirming the update was successfully applied, and the screen is subsequently refreshed to display the updated card details with a success confirmation message

sub_functionalities.title: Compare Current Database Values against Originally Fetched Values: CVV Code matches? Card Name matches? Expiry Year matches? Expiry Month matches? Expiry Day matches? Active Status matches?

rules.rule_name: BR-21.1.1: Normalize Card Name to Uppercase Before Concurrent Update Comparison
rules.rule_description: Before comparing the card record retrieved from the database against the values originally shown to the user, the cardholder name from the database must be converted to uppercase to ensure a case-insensitive, consistent comparison.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Convert Card Name from database to Uppercase for comparison

acceptance_criteria.Given: A card record has been retrieved from the database as part of the concurrent update check, and the cardholder name field (Card Embossed Name) may contain lowercase or mixed-case characters
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to compare the current database record against the values originally fetched and displayed to the user
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system converts all lowercase alphabetic characters in the Card Embossed Name retrieved from the database to uppercase before any field-level comparison is performed, ensuring the name comparison is case-insensitive

rules.rule_name: BR-21.1.2: Detect Concurrent Modification by Comparing All Card Fields Against Originally Fetched Values
rules.rule_description: The system performs a comprehensive six-field comparison between the current database record and the values originally displayed to the user to detect whether another user has modified the card record in the interim. All six fields must match for the update to be considered safe to proceed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: CVV Code in database matches originally fetched CVV Code? Card Name in database matches originally fetched Card Name? Expiry Year in database matches originally fetched Expiry Year? Expiry Month in database matches originally fetched Expiry Month? Expiry Day in database matches originally fetched Expiry Day? Active Status in database matches originally fetched Active Status?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has confirmed their changes and the system has successfully locked the card record for update, and the system holds the originally fetched values for: CVV Code, Card Name (uppercase), Expiry Year (positions 1-4 of expiry date), Expiry Month (positions 6-2 of expiry date), Expiry Day (positions 9-2 of expiry date), and Active Status
acceptance_criteria.When: The system compares the current database values against the originally fetched values across all six fields simultaneously: CVV Code, Card Name (after uppercase conversion), Expiry Year, Expiry Month, Expiry Day, and Active Status
acceptance_criteria.Then: If ALL six fields match between the current database record and the originally fetched values, the system determines that no concurrent modification has occurred and proceeds safely with the card update; if ANY one or more of the six fields do not match, the system determines that the record was changed by another user and cancels the current update attempt

rules.rule_name: BR-21.1.3: Allow Update to Proceed When No Concurrent Modification is Detected
rules.rule_description: When all six card fields in the current database record exactly match the values originally fetched and displayed to the user, the system confirms that no other user has modified the record and the pending update is safe to apply.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: All fields match - No concurrent changes detected - Safe to proceed with update

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has completed the six-field comparison between the current database record and the originally fetched values for CVV Code, Card Name, Expiry Year, Expiry Month, Expiry Day, and Active Status
acceptance_criteria.When: All six fields match exactly between the current database record and the originally fetched values (CVV Code matches AND Card Name matches AND Expiry Year matches AND Expiry Month matches AND Expiry Day matches AND Active Status matches)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the concurrent-change indicator to 'No Change Detected', confirms it is safe to proceed with writing the user's updates to the database, and continues with the card update write operation without interruption

rules.rule_name: BR-21.1.4: Flag Record as Concurrently Modified When Any Field Mismatch is Detected
rules.rule_description: If any one of the six compared fields (CVV Code, Card Name, Expiry Year, Expiry Month, Expiry Day, or Active Status) differs between the current database record and the values originally shown to the user, the system concludes that another user has modified the card record and the current update must be cancelled.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Record was changed by another user

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has completed the six-field comparison between the current database record and the originally fetched values
acceptance_criteria.When: At least one of the following mismatches is detected: CVV Code in the database does not match the originally fetched CVV Code, OR Card Name in the database (after uppercase conversion) does not match the originally fetched Card Name, OR Expiry Year in the database does not match the originally fetched Expiry Year, OR Expiry Month in the database does not match the originally fetched Expiry Month, OR Expiry Day in the database does not match the originally fetched Expiry Day, OR Active Status in the database does not match the originally fetched Active Status
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the concurrent-change indicator to 'Data Was Changed Before Update', marking that another user has modified the record since it was last displayed to the current user, and the current user's update attempt is cancelled

rules.rule_name: BR-21.1.5: Refresh Held Card Values with Latest Database Data After Concurrent Modification is Detected
rules.rule_description: When a concurrent modification is detected, the system replaces the previously held (originally fetched) card values with the latest values from the database, so that the most current data is available to be re-displayed to the user for review before they can attempt another update.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Refresh held values with latest data from database: CVV, Card Name, Expiry Date, Active Status

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has detected that the card record was modified by another user (concurrent modification flag is set to 'Data Was Changed Before Update')
acceptance_criteria.When: The system refreshes the held card values after detecting the concurrent modification
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system overwrites all six originally fetched held values with the latest values from the current database record: the held CVV Code is replaced with the database CVV Code, the held Card Name is replaced with the database Card Name (uppercase), the held Expiry Year is replaced with characters 1-4 of the database expiry date, the held Expiry Month is replaced with characters 6-2 of the database expiry date, the held Expiry Day is replaced with characters 9-2 of the database expiry date, and the held Active Status is replaced with the database Active Status; the update write operation is then immediately cancelled and control returns to the calling update process

rules.rule_name: BR-21.1.6: Re-Display Latest Card Details to User After Concurrent Modification Cancels Update
rules.rule_description: After a concurrent modification is detected and the update is cancelled, the program transitions the screen state to Show Details so that the user is presented with the latest card data from the database, allowing them to review the current values and decide whether to re-submit their changes.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: End: Return result - Data Changed = Yes - Proceed to update cancelled - Latest values shown to user

acceptance_criteria.Given: The write processing routine has returned with the concurrent-change indicator set to 'Data Was Changed Before Update', indicating that another user modified the card record before the current user's confirmed update could be saved
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the outcome of the write processing after the user pressed PF5 to confirm their changes
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the program display state to 'Show Details', causing the screen to be refreshed and re-displayed to the user with the latest card values retrieved from the database (the refreshed held values), so the user can see what the record currently contains before deciding to re-enter and re-confirm their changes
