The program manages the full update lifecycle including input validation, change detection, concurrency checking, and writing the updated record back to the card data file. It operates as a main/driver program, receiving control from a card list screen or main menu and transferring control back upon completion.
- **Execution Environment**: Online (CICS) - **Database Access**: VSAM/CICS File - **MQ Calls**: No - **Module Type**: Main module
### Key Functionalities: 1: Program Initialization - Initialize working storage areas, communication areas, and set default values at program entry 2: Communication Area Handling - Determine if program is being entered fresh or re-entered by checking EIBCALEN and source program, and load or initialize the communication area accordingly 3: PF Key Mapping and Validation - Map and store the pressed function key, then validate whether the key pressed is valid in the current context (Enter, PF03, PF05, PF12) 4: Exit and Navigation Control - When PF03 is pressed or update is complete/failed from card list screen, navigate back to the calling program (card list or main menu) passing context data 5: Fetch Card Details from Card List - When arriving from the credit card list screen, automatically retrieve card details using the account ID and card number passed from the list screen 6: Fresh Entry Screen Presentation - On first entry into the program, display a blank update screen prompting the user to enter account number and card number as search keys 7: Post-Update Screen Reset - After a successful or failed update, reset all search keys and program state, then present a fresh search screen to the user 8: User Input Processing - Receive and process user inputs from the screen, then validate those inputs and set the next program and map for navigation 9: Screen Data Reception - Receive the map input from the terminal, replacing asterisks and spaces with low-values for account ID, card number, card name, card status, expiry month, and expiry year fields 10: Account Number Validation - Validate that the account number is provided, is numeric, and is an 11-digit non-zero number; set appropriate error flags and messages if invalid 11: Card Number Validation - Validate that the card number is provided, is numeric, and is a 16-digit number; set appropriate error flags and messages if invalid 12: Search Criteria Completeness Check - Check if both account number and card number are blank and set a 'no search criteria received' message if neither is provided 13: Card Name Validation - Validate that the card name is provided and contains only alphabetic characters and spaces; set error flags and messages if invalid 14: Card Active Status Validation - Validate that the card active status is provided and is either 'Y' (active) or 'N' (inactive); set error flags and messages if invalid 15: Card Expiry Month Validation - Validate that the expiry month is provided, numeric, and between 1 and 12; set error flags and messages if invalid 16: Card Expiry Year Validation - Validate that the expiry year is provided, numeric, and between 1950 and 2099; set error flags and messages if invalid 17: Change Detection - Compare new card data entered by the user against the originally fetched card data to determine if any changes were actually made 18: Action Decision Logic - Based on current program state (details not fetched, details shown, changes made, changes confirmed, etc.) decide the next action to perform 19: Card Data Read for Display - Read the card record from the card database using the card number as the key to retrieve current card details for display 20: Card Data Preparation for Display - After successfully reading the card record, extract and store CVV, embossed name (converted to uppercase), expiry year, expiry month, expiry day, and active status into old-details holding area 21: Concurrent Update Detection - Before saving changes, re-read the card record and compare current database values against the originally fetched values to detect if another user has modified the record in the meantime 22: Card Record Update - Prepare the updated card record with new card name, expiry date (formatted as YYYY-MM-DD), active status, and CVV, then write the updated record back to the card database 23: Update Outcome Handling - After the write attempt, evaluate the outcome: set success status if update succeeded, or set appropriate failure status (lock error, update failed, or data changed by another user) 24: Screen Initialization - Initialize the output screen area, populate screen header with titles, transaction ID, program name, current date, and current time 25: Screen Variable Population - Populate screen fields with appropriate data based on current program state: show old values when displaying details, new values when changes are in progress, or blank values for fresh entry 26: Information Message Setup - Set the appropriate informational message based on program state: prompt for search keys, show card details found, prompt for changes, prompt for confirmation, confirm success, or inform failure 27: Screen Field Attribute Control - Set screen field attributes (protected/unprotected/editable) based on program state: account and card number fields are editable only when searching, card detail fields are editable only when updating 28: Cursor Positioning - Position the screen cursor on the appropriate field based on validation errors or program state to guide the user to the next required input 29: Screen Color Coding - Apply color attributes to screen fields: highlight fields with errors in red, apply default colors for fields coming from the card list screen, and highlight function key area when confirmation is needed 30: Screen Transmission - Send the formatted screen map to the terminal with cursor positioning and keyboard unlock 31: Program Return - Save error messages and communication area data, then return control to CICS with the current transaction ID and updated communication area for the next interaction
